thread:
devon: We're seeing failures in our Private deployment during model pulls and package installs after moving into our VPC. Error looks like TLS handshake / DNS timeouts. Example from the deploy log:
```
ERROR: could not fetch https://registry.redwood.ai/models/foo: TLS handshake timeout
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30000 ms
```
We also see apt and pip failing: `deb.debian.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org` fail intermittently. Can you provide a minimal egress allowlist we should request for security to open? We can't open wide CIDRs — prefer FQDN list. Also telemetry/auth endpoints need to be reachable (we're seeing 401s when tokens can't be validated). cc @anya @samir

anya: Sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the exact error from the model agent? Also which Private image (onprem-2025.11) and region? Do you have packet captures for DNS failures?

devon: Agent: `onprem-agent v2.3.1`. Region: eu-west-1 (customer-managed VPC). DNS logs show NXDOMAIN for `model-registry.redwood.ai` and TCP RST to `auth.redwood.ai:443`. We do have a TLS intercepting proxy in front of outbound 443 which breaks OCSP. Example curl with verbose:
```
* Connected to auth.redwood.ai (10.10.5.7) port 443
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* SSL peer certificate can't be authenticated by known CA.
```

samir: Ok — this looks like SNI/TLS interception issue plus some DNS rewrite. To unblock quickly, you can request allowlist for the following hostnames (FQDNs) and ports 443 (HTTPS) 80 (http) and 853 (DNS over TLS) where applicable:
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- models-storage.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- tokens.redwood.ai
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai
- telemetry.collect.redwood.ai
- registry-1.docker.io
- ghcr.io
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- deb.debian.org
- security.debian.org
- storage.googleapis.com (for some third-party model shards)
- s3.amazonaws.com (some customers may mirror packages)
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
- crl.globalsign.com
- crl.sectigo.com

Also allow outbound DNS to your resolver and don't rewrite SNI for the above hosts. If your TLS proxy performs certificate re-signing, configure it to bypass these hostnames so the agent can validate OCSP/CRL and upstream cert chains.

support-bot: Thanks — added to ticket RED-1245. @infra-team please confirm if we can provide IP ranges for infra-managed customers.

infra-team: For customers that require IP-based rules, we can provide region-specific CIDRs but note they can change. We prefer domain allowlists. If IPs are mandatory, request a weekly pull for updates. For immediate unblock, open egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on 443 temporarily while we validate domains (not recommended).

devon: Thanks. Can you also confirm telemetry URIs and whether token exchange uses `POST https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token`? We got 401s when proxying.

samir: Correct, token exchange is `https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token`. Telemetry ingestion endpoints are `https://telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai/v1/events` and `https://telemetry.collect.redwood.ai/v1/metrics`. If you keep TLS passthrough for those hosts it should stop the 401s. We'll update RED-1245 with these hostnames and a recommended SNI bypass config. :thumbsup:
